name: High-grade B-cell lymphoma with MYC and/or BCL2 and/or BCL6 rearrangement
aliases: High-grade B-cell lymphoma with rearrangements of MYC and BCL2 and/or BCL6

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: WHO Classification of Tumors of Hematopoietic and Lymphoid Tissues (2016)

criteria.description: Presence of large B-cell lymphoma morphology consistent with high-grade lymphoma
Detection of rearrangements involving MYC and/or BCL2 and/or BCL6 by FISH or other molecular techniques
Immunohistochemical expression of B-cell markers (CD19, CD20) and assessment of proliferation index (Ki-67 often >70%)
Exclusion of other lymphoma subtypes such as Burkitt lymphoma or diffuse large B-cell lymphoma without MYC/BCL2/BCL6 rearrangements

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Histopathological confirmation of high-grade B-cell lymphoma morphology plus demonstration of MYC and/or BCL2 and/or BCL6 rearrangements by molecular testing
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis requires integration of morphology, immunophenotyping, and genetic studies; clinical correlation is essential.

pathognomonic.notes: Typically involves cervical, axillary, or abdominal lymph nodes

pathognomonic.symptomName: B symptoms (fever, night sweats, weight loss)

common.symptomName: Extranodal involvement (e.g., gastrointestinal tract, bone marrow)
common.notes: Common sites include stomach and intestines
searchTerms: disease outside lymph nodes like gut or marrow
involvement of organs beyond lymph nodes
spread to bone marrow or intestines

common.notes: Enlargement of liver and spleen due to infiltration

searchTerms: fatigue related to low red blood cells

occasional.symptomName: Central nervous system involvement symptoms (e.g., headache, cranial nerve palsies)
occasional.notes: Occurs in advanced or relapsed disease
searchTerms: headache and nerve palsies from CNS disease
neurological symptoms like cranial nerve weakness

occasional.notes: Due to lymphomatous infiltration or secondary causes

occasional.symptomName: Skin lesions due to cutaneous involvement

occasional.notes: May indicate bone marrow or cortical bone infiltration

rare.notes: Due to tumor secretion of parathyroid hormone-related protein
Metabolic emergency from rapid tumor cell breakdown
searchTerms: chemical imbalance from cancer cell death
tumor lysis causing kidney and electrolyte problems

imaging: PET-CT showing hypermetabolic lymphadenopathy and extranodal lesions
CT scans revealing organomegaly and mass lesions
other: High Ki-67 proliferation index (>70%) on immunohistochemistry
Immunophenotyping positive for CD19, CD20, CD10 (variable)

distinguishingFeatures: Absence of MYC and BCL2/BCL6 rearrangements
MYC rearrangement without BCL2 or BCL6 rearrangements

redFlags: Rapidly progressive lymphadenopathy with systemic symptoms
references: Swerdlow SH, Campo E, Harris NL, et al. WHO Classification of Tumours of Haematopoietic and Lymphoid Tissues. IARC; 2016.
